articles.title: Caitlin Clark's Nike Caitlin 1 sneakers work “magic” with Pat McAfee after she debuted them at home
articles.standfirst: Caitlin Clark's first signature shoe has officially arrived, and Pat McAfee's playful reaction provided another memorable moment during her return to Iowa City
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark's first signature shoe has officially arrived, and Pat McAfee's playful reaction provided another memorable moment during her return to Iowa City
articles.body:
C aitlin Clark may have seen her WNBA season come to an earlier end than she wanted, but the Indiana Fever star has wasted little time finding another way to make headlines.

Clark returned to Iowa City on Saturday as a guest picker on ESPN's College GameDay, appearing alongside Pat McAfee and the rest of the show's crew before Iowa hosted Ohio State.

The former Hawkeye was back in familiar surroundings just days after Indiana was eliminated from the WNBA playoffs by the Las Vegas Aces .

Rather than simply talk college football, Clark also used the opportunity to showcase something that has been years in the making: her first signature basketball shoe with Nike.

The Nike Caitlin 1 officially launched globally on October 1, making the College GameDay appearance one of Clark's first major public opportunities to promote the sneakers following their release.

Nike describes the shoe as being designed around the qualities that define Clark's game, including her speed, shooting range and ability to change direction unpredictably.

Clark arrived in Iowa City wearing a sparkling version of the sneakers and encouraged fans to check them out. Her message was partly promotional and partly a joke directed toward McAfee , who had already tried a pair himself.

“Come on!.. I brought super sparkly… Pat said they’re even super comfortable, even if you don’t play ball, go get them,” Clark said during the segment.

McAfee had apparently already conducted his own test.

The former NFL punter revealed that he had worn the Caitlin 1s the previous night and was impressed by how they felt. His assessment became particularly entertaining when he connected the footwear to his performance on a basketball court.

“I have fat feet. I wore them last night. They were comfortable. I went down to the basketball court down there and got absolutely wet from the logo,” McAfee said during the segment.

The exchange gave Clark an easy way to highlight one of the selling points of the shoe beyond its connection to her basketball career: comfort.

Caitlin Clark has been building anticipation for the Caitlin 1

The timing of the College GameDay appearance is significant because the Caitlin 1 is no longer simply an upcoming product. It is now available to consumers, with Nike listing the shoe in the UK at £129.99, while the U.S. launch price is $140.

Nike's design places considerable emphasis on Clark's playing style. The shoe uses an Opticast upper designed to provide lightweight support, while a forefoot Air Zoom Turbo unit and Cushlon foam are intended to provide responsive cushioning.

The design also includes Clark -specific touches such as her CC logo, references to her No. 22 jersey and stacked Swoosh detailing.

Clark has also been promoting the sneakers in a much more personal way.

Before the public release, she gave pairs to her Fever teammates, turning the locker room into something of an unofficial preview for the product.

After Indiana defeated the Dallas Wings in August, Clark surprised teammates with Nike shoes that included unreleased Caitlin 1s. Tyasha Harris captured the excitement on social media, writing that “Christmas came early.”

She repeated the gesture following Team USA's gold-medal run at the FIBA Women's World Cup in September, handing out unreleased Racer Blue versions when she returned to the Fever locker room.

Makayla Timpson 's reaction became one of the memorable moments from the videos shared online: “Going global in these shoes.”

Those moments have helped create interest around the Caitlin 1 without relying exclusively on traditional advertising. Having Clark's teammates receive and react to the shoes gives fans a glimpse of the product in a genuine basketball environment.

That is particularly useful for a first signature shoe, because the Caitlin 1 is more than another piece of Clark merchandise.

It represents a significant milestone in her relationship with Nike and places her among a relatively small group of active basketball players with their own signature footwear.

The release also comes at an interesting point in Clark's career.

Her 2026 WNBA season ended in the first round when the Fever fell 94-83 to the Aces in Game 3. Clark finished that game with 18 points, while A'ja Wilson produced 36 points and 10 rebounds to send Las Vegas through to the semifinals.

Yet the end of Indiana's campaign has not stopped Clark's momentum away from the court. Her College GameDay appearance brought her back to the place where her national profile first exploded, while the launch of the Caitlin 1 gives her another major platform outside the WNBA.

And McAfee's reaction only added to the fun.

Whether the Caitlin 1 can become a long-term success will ultimately depend on how basketball players respond to it, but Clark has already given Nike plenty of attention around its launch.

For now, her playful exchange with McAfee has provided another piece of publicity for a shoe that is designed to reflect exactly how Clark wants her game to be remembered: fast, confident and willing to shoot from anywhere.

articles.title: Where to watch Atlanta Dream vs New York Liberty and what is the kickoff time for Angel Reese’s Semifinals Game?
articles.standfirst: Dream host Liberty in a Semifinal showdown as Atlanta looks to finish what September Started
articles.summary: Dream host Liberty in a Semifinal showdown as Atlanta looks to finish what September Started
articles.body:
The WNBA Playoffs have reached their defining stretch, and few matchups carry the weight of what unfolds at Gateway Center Arena when the Atlanta Dream welcome the New York Liberty.

Two of the Eastern Conference's standard-bearers arrive riding momentum from first-round sweeps, and the familiarity between them is anything but incidental — these clubs met twice in the final week of the regular season, and both of those meetings went Atlanta's way.

Atlanta Dream vs New York Liberty: Schedule and where to watch game 1

Tip-off for the Atlanta Dream vs New York Liberty game 1 is set for Sunday, October 4, 2026, at 1:00 p.m. Eastern Time (12:00 p.m. Central Time and 10:00 a.m. Pacific Time), at Gateway Center Arena in Atlanta , a compact 3,500-seat venue that should be loud from the opening possession.

You can catch the action across the WNBA Playoffs on different networks; and for this particular semifinals game you’ll be able to watch it on ESPN and fubo, DirecTV and the ESPN app on streaming.

How do Atlanta Dream and New York Liberty got here

Atlanta enters as the hotter team and the higher seed. The Dream finished atop the Eastern Conference at 30-14 , fourth overall in the league, and have barely broken stride since. They dispatched the Washington Mystics in their opening playoff series, winning 92-77 at home and then closing it out 93-75 on the road.

Stretch that back further and the picture is even more daunting for New York: Atlanta has reeled off a lengthy run of victories, including that September pair against the Liberty — a 95-84 road win on September 22 and an 83-65 statement on September 24.

New York, seeded fourth in the East at 26-18 (eighth overall), answered the doubts in emphatic fashion. Drawn against the top-seeded Minnesota Lynx — the best regular-season team in the league at 33-11 — the Liberty flipped the script, winning 91-75 in Minnesota and then 87-71 at home to eliminate the conference's No. 1 overall seed.

For a team that stumbled through an inconsistent regular season, that was a resounding reminder of their ceiling.

The Atlanta Dream vs New York Liberty H2H subplot

The timing of their recent meetings sharpens the storyline. Atlanta beat New York twice in the span of 48 hours in late September, and the margins grew: an 11-point win followed by an 18-point handling.

Those results matter, but postseason basketball resets emotion, and the Liberty's upset of Minnesota suggests this is a different group than the one that lost back-to-back games just over a week earlier.

What is the prediction for the Atlanta Dream vs New York Liberty games?

Everything points toward a tight, physical contest. Atlanta owns the recent results, the home floor, and the better regular-season body of work, and the Dream's defense has looked playoff-sharp.

But New York's demolition of the No. 1 seed can't be ignored — this is a team peaking at the right time. Expect Atlanta to protect home court in a close, hard-fought game, with Gray and Reese proving the difference on the glass and down the stretch. The Dream to edge it, but don't be surprised if the Liberty make it a nervy finish.

Atlanta enters as the hotter team and the higher seed. The Dream finished atop the Eastern Conference at 30-14 , fourth overall in the league, and have barely broken stride since. The timing of their recent meetings sharpens the storyline. Atlanta beat New York twice in the span of 48 hours in late September, and the margins grew: an 11-point win followed by an 18-point handling.

Those results matter, but postseason basketball resets emotion, and the Liberty's upset of Minnesota suggests this is a different group than the one that lost back-to-back games just over a week earlier.

Everything points toward a tight, physical contest. Atlanta owns the recent results, the home floor, and the better regular-season body of work, and the Dream's defense has looked playoff-sharp.

Expect Atlanta to protect home court in a close, hard-fought game, with Gray and Reese proving the difference on the glass and down the stretch. The Dream to edge it, but don't be surprised if the Liberty make it a nervy finish.

articles.title: Kelsey Mitchell reveals problems with Indiana Fever and may leave because of Caitlin Clark
articles.standfirst: Mitchell is entering unrestricted free agency after another impressive season in Indiana
articles.summary: Mitchell is entering unrestricted free agency after another impressive season in Indiana
articles.body:
K elsey Mitchell 's future with the Indiana Fever has suddenly become one of the biggest questions of the WNBA offseason, and her latest comments have offered an unusually candid look at what it is like to play alongside Caitlin Clark .

Mitchell has spent her entire WNBA career in Indiana after being selected No.2 overall in the 2018 draft.

For years, she was the centerpiece of a struggling franchise, carrying much of the offensive responsibility before the Fever eventually landed Aliyah Boston and Clark with consecutive No.1 picks. Now, however, the 30-year-old guard is an unrestricted free agent.

Her comments following Indiana's playoff elimination suggested that her decision will involve much more than money or basketball.

“Showing up every day to compete for fans that may or may not like you is hard. I don’t think people understand that,” Mitchell said at the Fever's end-of-season press conference.

She then explained how playing alongside Clark has brought an additional layer of attention to every member of the Indiana roster.

“I think having to show up for people that don’t look at you and have, you know, the star eyes when they see me," Mitchell said. "But playing with CC and having the eyes that she got, we get a lot of flak just for being on her team.

"So I think that comes with a lot too, and I think that people gotta give us grace. I think that this organization is unbelievable, man, but I think that when it comes to really trying to be yourself, it hasn’t always been easy. That’s all I’ll say."

Mitchell 's remarks may not amount to a declaration that she wants to leave the Fever. In fact, she has repeatedly spoken positively about the organization and her teammates.

But they do demonstrate that the enormous attention surrounding Clark has affected the wider group.

Free agency decision comes after career-best season

The timing is particularly significant because Mitchell has arguably never been more valuable to Indiana.

She averaged 24.7 points per game during the 2026 regular season, shooting 50.9% from the field and 45.0% from three-point range. She played all 44 regular-season games and became one of the league's most productive offensive players.

Her postseason performances were strong, too. Mitchell scored 26 points in Indiana's 99-89 Game 2 victory over Las Vegas to force a decisive matchup, before leading the Fever again with 23 points in the season-ending 94-83 defeat.

The Fever ultimately lost the first-round series 2-1, ending a season in which Indiana finished 28-16 and earned the No.6 seed. That means Mitchell heads into free agency with significant leverage.

She has also made it clear that she intends to consider what is best for her rather than automatically returning to the franchise where she has spent nine seasons.

“I think I have to be selfish. I think that’s where I am in my career, about what I probably need and what's probably best for me," Mitchell said.

“I've got to be selfish where my career is going, in terms of what's important to me. Whether it be winning, whether it be my own individual success.

"I worked my tail off to be here, so whatever I do, it's gonna come from a selfish standpoint. I'll be honest about that.”

Fever general manager Amber Cox has made no secret of the organization's desire to retain Mitchell, saying that the team hopes to keep her in Indiana for the remainder of her career.

“I mean, Kelsey is obviously a major priority. She has a lot of equity in this franchise and has put in a lot of time,” Cox said. She also indicared the Fever hope to build on the partnership between Mitchell and Clark .

The difficulty is that Mitchell 's concerns go beyond basketball. The Fever have been surrounded by controversy throughout the season, with incidents involving fans, opposing players and social-media criticism repeatedly becoming part of the conversation.

During the playoffs, A'ja Wilson confronted a fan during Game 2, while other incidents involving Fever games had already generated significant attention. Mitchell said the online side of the experience has been particularly difficult.

“I don’t think people really understand how much we endured,” she added. “If I showed y’all my DMs about the hate and all of the stuff that comes with being a professional athlete but specifically being an Indiana Fever basketball player, it’s a lot that goes into that.”

Those comments stand in contrast with Cox 's defense of the Fever fanbase. The general manager said that “attacks on our fan base have no basis in reality,” creating an obvious difference in how the experience is being perceived by the players and the front office.

That divide could become an important part of the offseason conversation. Still, it would be premature to conclude that Mitchell is leaving because of Clark .

The two have developed into one of the WNBA's most productive scoring combinations, and their partnership has been a major reason for Indiana's improvement.

The Fever also have a clear incentive to retain an elite veteran who can shoot at a high level while taking some of the offensive burden away from Clark . Mitchell , meanwhile, has earned the right to examine every option.

After nine seasons with one franchise, a career-best statistical year and a growing role alongside one of the sport's biggest stars, her decision will likely come down to what environment she believes best fits the next stage of her career.

For the Fever , keeping Mitchell would preserve the core of a team that believes it can eventually compete for a championship. For Mitchell , however, her latest comments make clear that basketball will not be the only consideration.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham gets the royal treatment in Missouri as fans welcome her home
articles.summary: Missouri gave Sophie Cunningham a warm welcome when the WNBA star returned to her alma mater for Mizzou Homecoming.
articles.body: Missouri gave Sophie Cunningham a warm welcome when the WNBA star returned to her alma mater for Mizzou Homecoming. Cunningham rode through the celebration in the bed of a pickup truck, waving to fans and tossing candy to children gathered along the parade route. The enthusiastic reception quickly drew attention on social media, where fans treated the former Tigers star like Missouri royalty. Cunningham remains Mizzou women's basketball's all-time leading scorer and was inducted into the university's athletic Hall of Fame in 2025. The celebration came shortly after Cunningham's second season with the Indiana Fever ended with a first-round playoff elimination. Her one-year contract expired, making her an unrestricted free agent ahead of the 2027 season. Her WNBA future may be uncertain, but in Missouri, Cunningham looked completely at home.
